string.text: Can you tell me anything interesting about this place?

Anything interesting? Well, I’m pretty new here myself, so I’m not really in the loop. Tell me, have you met Toad yet? 

He’s a greedy bastard, who charges triple for everything, but what can you do? He knows that the next closest trader is at the Bar, and not everyone can make it that far. Besides, word is that the traders there only deal with stalkers who’ve already made a name for themselves. 

As for Toad, well, he might be a "toad," but he’ll sell to anyone. Just don’t expect to walk away feeling happy about the deal.

Here, take a look. I’ll show you on my PDA. 

That’s a military checkpoint; don’t even think about going near it. In fact, it’s best to stay out of the military’s sight altogether. Now see that spot on the hill? Looks like an old boiler house. It’s better to give that a wide berth, too. And over by the bridge, there’s some kind of building, but mutants hang around nearby, so it’s best to steer clear. 

To the west, past the bridge, there’s an old hamlet. It’s a very dangerous place, so I’d advise avoiding it. But here, by the road, there’s a small, old house; it’s a decent stopover if you’re heading toward the trader or the Garbage. 

That’s all I know.

There’s nothing interesting here, and no loot to be found. Just a lot of soldiers, the brainless freaks. Take my advice: stay out of their sight. They’ll gun you down without batting an eye. \n\nToad claims he’s got everything under control, but that’s complete bullshit. He’s not protecting us from the military — he’s protecting the military from us. If a soldier gets killed, there’ll be hell to pay. But if a stalker dies? They’ll just bury him in the bushes, if he’s even worth that much; more likely, they’ll just feed him to the mutants and be done with it.

You’re asking the wrong person. I’m new here myself. Seen any anomalies yet? You know, those things that look like patches of colored fog? 

Once, through my binoculars, I saw a blind dog fly straight into one. They were hunting a boar as a pack, and one of them… I don’t know, got carried away? I’m not sure how these they sense anomalies, but that one clearly missed it. It was a horrific sight—and the squealing! Absolutely chilling. 

I don’t even want to get close to those anomalies, and I’d advise you to stay away, too.

What’s so interesting here? It’s deadly dull. You know, I’m thinking of heading to the Garbage. From there, it’s just a stone’s throw to the Center of the Zone. And they say that in the Center, you can find the Wish Granter. \n\nAnyway, you’d be better off not lingering here. There’s nothing for you to do other than to just slave away for that old geezer, Toad, who pays next to nothing.

Watch out for the choppers. I heard some fool climbed onto a bridge and opened fire on one, talk about a genius, right? The military didn’t hesitate to waste a missile on him. Didn’t leave a trace of the idiot behind.

Everything here is interesting — this is the Zone, after all! Just look around: anomalies, creatures unknown to science, and absolute freedom. No one tells you what to do! \n\nI’ve heard that many stalkers come here looking for riches, only to end up staying forever. And I can see why. Out there, beyond the perimeter, it’s all boredom, dreariness, and filth. But here? Now this is real life!

The Zone itself is fascinating. Everywhere you look, there’s something interesting to see. Just the other day, I managed to snag my first artifact. It was a small, trivial thing. Toad just cursed when he saw it. But he still tossed some cash my way. Ever seen an artifact yourself? Exactly — it’s a whole different level of interesting! You get to turn some anomalous trinket over in your hands, and maybe even walk away with a brand-new rifle to show for it. \n\nTrue, so far, I’ve only earned enough for some canned food and a bottle of vodka, but hey, as the saying goes, what’s a small step for humanity is a giant leap for an ordinary stalker, right? That’s how I see it, anyway.

That’s an interesting point... I don’t know if you’d call it "interesting," but there’s a derailed locomotive to the right of the bridge. it’s a great landmark for crossing over to the other side. Military patrols don’t go there. Feel free to use it. \n\nJust don’t go shooting at the chopper, alright? We had one "special" guy here a while back who tried that. You don’t look like that kind of idiot, but who knows?

Run into any bandits yet? Real scumbags, the lot of them. They band together and make a living by shaking people down. They’re too chicken to venture into the anomalies themselves, but they’ve got no problem stripping a fellow stalker of his gear. If you see that trash, shoot first, don’t even think twice. 

It’s a bit calmer around here now, thankfully. There used to be a gang operating in these parts—had an interesting name, something like "Cowboys"... or maybe "The Men with No Name"? No, it was named after a brand of cigarettes... "Camel"? "Parliament"? Ah, forget it, it doesn't matter. 

Anyway, they were a nasty bunch, but they had a whole system set up. They’d set ambushes, take your weapons, and send you packing with a parting line: "Bring us the cash, and you’ll get your gun back." 

Eventually, they got into a dispute with some diggers, and the diggers gave them a proper thrashing. Haven’t seen those diggers around in a long time, though — which means the "Cowboys" might just come back. Keep your guard up.

All the really interesting stuff is further ahead, up North. Think of this place as a testing ground—a little "amusement park" within the Zone. There aren’t too many anomalies around here, the mutants aren’t the most dangerous, and there’s a trader close by. Up North, it’s a completely different story—anomalies are crawling everywhere, the mutants are as hideous as Toad’s mother (may the Lord rest her soul) and the nearest trader can be a day’s journey away, if not more. \n\nAnd if you don’t have access to the Bar, well, you’ll have to trek all the way back to Toad himself.

Have you heard about the local legend? You know, the fool who opened fire on a military chopper? They say Toad nearly kicked the bucket — his heart gave out from the shock. Word is, he went to the military in person afterward to beg for forgiveness on behalf of all the stalkers, and ever since then, the suitcases of cash he sends them have gotten a lot heavier. 

As for the lad himself — it’s a pity. I don’t know what got into him, but there wasn’t even a PDA left behind. Nobody even knows his name. I didn’t know him personally, either; this happened before my time. 

Anyway, take note—learn from other people’s mistakes.

I heard that not long ago, a truck crashed somewhere around here—a rather curious truck, at that. And rumor has it they found a just as curious passenger inside... \n\nThe whole Zone is buzzing about it.

Ever heard of "diggers"? No? That’s a shame. Snitch tipped me off that they had a stash somewhere around here, packed with all sorts of loot. They’ve been gone a long time, so they won’t be needing any of it, but I certainly could use it. \n\nHmm… looks like you really don’t have a clue. Forget I said anything. But if I ever find out that you were looking for this stash too, you’re going to regret it. Got that?

It’s not the place that’s interesting here; it’s the people. Just think about it: the perimeter is practically a stone’s throw away. This is where "greenhorns", full of anticipation for wealth and the fulfillment of their deepest wishes, slip into the Zone. And it’s also where the old-timers leave — often with no riches to show for it, their wishes left unfulfilled. Everyone has their own story, their own comedy, their own tragedy. Just like in the tales of the ancient Greeks, get it? 

A stalker, nearing the end of his time here, might sit by the campfire with the new arrivals, share a few jokes and tall tales, offer some parting advice to the next generation, and then leave the Zone for good. But his legacy lives on in the minds and hearts of those who shared that final meal with him. 

In a single word: romance.

A rookie, are you? You certainly don’t look like one. So, how are you with a map? I suspect you’ve already met Toad, and he’s likely talked your ear off about the military checkpoint, so we’ll skip that part. 

Listen, there’s a military patrol moving between the checkpoint and the bridge — best not to let them spot you. If things get dicey, dive into the bushes and keep quiet; they’ve got an arrangement with Toad — they’ll look the other way. 

There’s a pipe (a drainage pipe, probably) on the left side of the embankment. You could use it to get to the other side, but I wouldn’t recommend it. There are mutants on both ends, and sometimes, after a blowout, an anomaly pops up in there. You wouldn’t be able to get through without an anomaly discharger. Over here, by the bridge, there’s an old water pumping station. Mutants wander in there quite often, so hardly anyone ever goes near it. If you need to get under the bridge but run into a patrol, you can wait it out there until they move on; you’ve got a good view from the roof. 

Off to the right, there’s an old factory — nothing worth finding there, though; anything of value was scavenged long ago. Beyond that lies a large field of anomalies. 

Oh, and one more thing: there’s an old house between the bridge and the northern gate. It’s a decent spot to stop and rest if you need to. 

Well, I suppose that’s about it.

You know what I find interesting? Toad might be a real wheeler-dealer, sure, but he does a lot for us, fellow stalkers. And nobody ever gives him any credit. People call him a greedy ass, an old geezer, and all that, but without him, this safe little haven in the village wouldn't even exist — and the military would be picking off stalkers left and right. \n\nSo, show the old man some respect, and be glad we’ve got him around.

There’s an interesting story from back when I was still a total greenhorn. Toad had this sharp kid working as a runner for him — a guy named Sashka Lucky" Well, one day, Lucky ran into some serious bad luck. 

He was carrying a delivery for Toad to that old house by the road and he always took the path past the locomotive; you know the one? Anyway, Sashka happened to stumble right into a pack of boars, so he took off, running blind. He scrambled up the embankment, and suddenly — bam! A helicopter pops up right in front of him! 

How can a helicopter just "pop up" when its rotors make so much noise? Well, you know how it is. When you’re pumped full of adrenaline with a pack of boars on your tail, your mind is on other things. So, Sashka sees something jump out in front of him and, on pure instinct, just opens fire blindly. The pilots must have been just as spooked, because one of them accidentally fired a rocket — and it hit the boars dead on! The boars were turned into mincemeat in an instant, and the shockwave threw Lucky right into the locomotive, smashing his PDA to bits in the process. You can’t even imagine what happened after that. Toad was absolutely furious! He was tearing his hair out, while Lucky wasn’t responding to any of his signals. On top of that, the military command demanded a massive sum in compensation; every single one of their missiles is accounted for, after all. 

And then the very next day, Lucky turned up — alive and well. Toad grabbed him, hauled him off to the checkpoint, and practically threw himself at the military's feet, begging for mercy. I don’t know exactly what they discussed with them, but Sashka is still out there somewhere, trekking across the Zone; Toad’s business is thriving; and those pilots, as far as I heard, even got some medals. Oh, and the helicopter flies a different route now. They set the course further east to avoid passing over the locomotive. 

That’s the story.

Hey, man. What are you doing coming to the Zone at your age? Then again, maybe it’s for the best; you get to see the Zone in its least dangerous state. You can take a look, realize you had no business coming here in the first place, make the right choice, and head back to the normal, non-stalker life.

I’m not really up to speed on the latest events. I just came down from the North to take care of some business—you’d be better off asking the locals; they’ll be able to tell you more. \n\nActually, tell me this: do you know anything about the local diggers? No? Well, then there’s nothing for us to talk about.

You don’t look like a rookie, so why are you asking questions like that? It’s just a place like any other. The rookies come here to get their bearings before heading deeper into the Zone, and the old-timers drop by when they’ve got business to attend to. You know what? Let me tell you about a certain tactic instead. 

Anomalies are our enemies, but they’re also enemies to mutants — and the enemy of your enemy is sometimes your friend. Some mutants avoid anomalies, which means you can use those anomalies to escape their territory. Others charge straight through and anomalies gobble them up for lunch without even breaking a sweat. But if you’re incredibly lucky, an anomaly might just choke and "burp up" an artifact for you as a thank-you for the snack. 

Good luck, use your head, and don’t forget to keep the type of the anomaly in mind.

Ever heard of the "death trucks"? It’s one of the Zone’s many mysteries. These trucks come barreling out from somewhere deep within the Zone’s center. 

To what end? Who knows. Who sends them? That’s a mystery, too. They’re always crashing, as if reaching a destination isn’t the point at all; as if the journey itself is the whole purpose…

I heard one of them crashed somewhere nearby; might be worth checking out.

The military guys at this checkpoint? They’re nothing to worry about. Just regular folks, they’ve got to eat, too. But deeper in the Zone, you’ll run into specialized military-stalker units: absolute scum, with, for crying out loud, color-coded call signs. \n\nIf you spot any little green men… or blue ones, or red ones, or whatever other colors they’ve got; get the hell out of there. For them, killing stalkers is nothing more than a sport.

The railway embankment runs into a mysterious, blocked-off tunnel, and nobody knows where it leads. Logic suggests it must go to the Garbage, but the tunnel is blocked on that end, too, so no one’s ever been able to verify that theory. From there, the tunnel most likely leads to the Agroprom Research Institute… 

Doesn’t sound all that interesting, but think about it. Why are those railway tracks even there? What were they hauling along them? And why? 

Someone ought to dig them up, but who’d ever take on a job like that?

Ever heard about that "idiot" — the one who supposedly took a potshot at a chopper, only to get vaporized for his trouble? It’s all a load of rubbish. How do I know? Simple: it was me. 

Back then, I was running errands for Toad. I was delivering a package to a stalker waiting in a house by the road. As luck would have it, I ran into a pack of fleshes. I would’ve gunned them all down, but my pistol jammed; that greedy bastard Toad had skimped on the weapon. So, with no other choice, I tried to clear the jam on the fly, but ended up stumbling right into an embankment. Realizing what was happening, I scrambled up the slope while the mutants squealed below, having lost their prey. 

Once I reached the top, I came face-to-face with a military chopper. I thought I was a goner, but the crew clearly hadn’t expected to see me and hesitated. I fired two precise shots at the pilots and took them both out. But, damn it all, the bodies of those idiots slumped onto the controls, and the chopper came hurtling straight at me! I barely managed to dive to the ground before it slammed into a locomotive, sending both of them tumbling off the embankment; and then the ammo detonated! 

It was absolute hell. Nothing was left of those mutants, and thanks to me, the stalkers ended up with a brand-new path. So, there you have it.
Look, pal, think about who you’re asking these questions to. Go pester some of the greenhorns hanging around here instead—I’ve got no time for you right now.

What’s so interesting here? Hell if I know; I haven’t been here in ages, and everything’s changed since then. What do you think — how often does a master-level stalker even wander into these parts? Last time I was here, the bridge was still standing. Or maybe it wasn’t… \n\nLook, man, just drop it; enough with the questions.

Jeez, you’re a grown man, yet you ask questions like some greenhorn. You’d be better off asking the locals; they’ll tell you more about this place than I ever could. 

But I can tell you something else — ever heard of the "Dark Stalkers"? It’s a faction in the Zone, a very mysterious one. Word is, they’ve been spotted around here lately. What could they possibly be looking for? 

If you run into any shady characters, it’s best to steer clear.

It’s nice here, you know? Up North, people have grown cold and hardened, but here, you can still find dreamers: folks whose souls haven’t been tainted by the harsh reality of the Zone. Enjoy it while you can.

Doesn’t look like anything interesting is happening here these days; not long ago, things were completely different. The last time I came back here… well, it’s been a while, can’t even remember exactly, but it’s been at least a month. 

Some local diggers were organizing a raid on a group of bandits, and since I happened to be at the Garbage, I decided to give them a hand. We really gave those guys a thrashing. 

Nobody remembers those diggers anymore, I suppose; or the bandits, for that matter. How many generations of stalkers have passed through here since then? 

Around here, you could say every newcomer represents a whole new generation. One passes on knowledge from those who came before, then moves on. So much is forgotten in a matter of days. Life here is fleeting, truly fleeting.

There’s nothing of interest here — at least, not for me. Or, at any rate, there wasn’t until recently. 

I’m looking for the Death Truck; or, rather, what’s left of it. It ought to be somewhere nearby. Do you happen to know where it is? No? I didn’t think so. 

Well, I’d best keep searching.

Actually, everything here is interesting — it is the Zone, after all. The deeper you go, the more fascinating (and dangerous) it becomes. 

Over the years, that sense of wonder dulls; you start to get used to the Zone’s little "tricks." But just when things get boring; when the daily grind of a stalker starts to feel routine — the Zone throws up new marvels to surprise you all over again. Even here, on the outskirts, you can always find something of interest. 

So, keep your eyes peeled and take it all in. It’s an unforgettable, irreplaceable feeling.

These piles of trash, these ruins—who knows what’s still hidden inside them? But you’d have to be a brainless scarecrow or a tin man made out of lead to dig through all this without worrying about kicking the bucket from radiation.

It’s absolute hell here: either you’re hounded by beasts, or you run into some thugs. The "Duty" faction has an outpost to the north; they seem like decent guys, but they don’t bother keeping order in the area. "Not our concern," they say. Still, they’re always ready to watch your back, so I suppose that’s something.

I haven’t been here long. People said there were artifacts galore, and maybe that’s true, but you won’t find much without a solid supply of anti-radiation meds. And whatever you do manage to find, you’ll just end up spending the profit on more anti-rads. I guess all you can do is hope an artifact happens to roll down one of these trash heaps on its own.

It’s a dump, just piles of junk everywhere, thugs roaming around looking for easy targets, and then there are the mutants... What is it with these dogs and these heaps of rust? There’s clearly nothing to eat there. \n\nI’m already missing Toad and sitting around the campfire with his bunch of layabouts. But I’m not turning back; I’ll convince the "Duty" guys to let me through to the Bar.

I don’t even know what to tell you, man. I heard there was a manhunt here for some psycho who was taking out stalkers for no reason at all. Of all the places, I never expected to run into a homicidal maniac here in the Zone.
What do you make of that locomotive by the ruins? Have you seen it yet? And how on earth did it end up there? The railway tracks are quite a distance away. Did a hurricane blow it in there?

There’s a large hangar in the center — a shady spot, best not to linger there. It keeps changing hands; good luck guessing whether it’s occupied by bandits or fellow stalkers today. I’ve always wondered, though: you can see a crane cab through a hole in the roof. Think there’s anything inside? I’m really curious, but I’d never climb up there myself. I’m afraid of heights.

Music. Well, not exactly music, more of a melody. Stop and listen. The piles of rusted wreckage seem to breathe, creaking and singing, accompanied by the howling of mutants, the shouts of stalkers, the sound of gunfire, and the cawing of crows. This place is one big orchestra. Hear what I mean?

A dumping ground for radioactive waste, brought here after the first disaster. Looters stripped away anything of value long before the second one; all that’s left is rusted scrap, which, for some godforsaken reason, seems to attract both mutants and anomalies. So, keep your eyes peeled; let your guard down for a second, and snap — some set of jaws clamps shut around your neck. And that’s that; you’re history.

This is the main artery of the southern Zone. Stalkers fan out from here in all directions — some head for the Agroprom Research Institute, others toward the Dark Valley, while the rookies stick around the Garbage to scrape together a living. They all end up back here eventually; there’s no other way to reach the traders. That’s why every two-bit gang and thug flocks to this place; wipe out one gang, and another immediately takes its spot. All in all, it’s a dangerous place to be.

It’s a crossroads here. Just like in a fairy tale: go one way, and you’ll end up at Agroprom; go another, and you’ll find yourself in the Dark Valley. And if you happen to catch the eye of the Duty faction, they might just let you, brave soul that you are, into the Bar.

It’s like a museum here, dedicated to the Chernobyl disaster. Everywhere you look, there are monuments to a bygone era, rooted deep into the earth. And these tunnels… they’re strange. Whoever built them clearly went to great lengths to ensure no one could ever use them again. They’ve been sealed up so thoroughly you’d need a crew of miners to get through. You chip away a brick, and behind it there’s solid concrete. It’s as if the entire tunnel has been filled to the brim.

Not long ago, an entire squad from the Duty faction met their end right here. Seen the messages online? Keep your eyes peeled. Whatever killed those guys is still out there… and it’s bound to be damn dangerous.

Nothing much to tell, really. Just heaps of trash — some spots are as radioactive as the reactor itself. Yet they still draw in the occasional "climber." To the south, there are the ruins of some building; the sewer system behind it is a favorite hideout for thugs. In the center, there’s a large hangar. Sometimes stalkers stop there to rest, other times some lowlifes try to set up a base. Up north, the “Duty” faction guards the road to the Bar; they act like pompous peacocks, but they won’t leave you in the lurch if things go south. To the west lies Agroprom, and to the east, the Dark Valley. That’s about it.

Cosmonaut met his end somewhere around here. He sent out an SOS, then, right before a blowout, he posted something in the chat about how beautiful the sky looks from up high; and that was it. Silence ever since. Strange last words, though he was always a bit of a romantic. \n\nAnyway, keep your eyes sharp. Cosmonaut was an experienced stalker who’d been trekking through the Zone for years, but one run-in with Ferret, and poof, he’s gone. Word is, you’ve crossed paths with Ferret, too. Why are you staring like that? It’s rare for anyone to make it out of those death trucks alive; the whole Zone is watching your exploits now.

Military stalkers have been spotted around here. They’ve wandered pretty far south… but why? Their units usually operate way up north, so this is unexpected. Could the military command be planning to get their hands on the Garbage? In that case, you can kiss the stalker life goodbye; the only way left to reach the Bar would be via Yantar, coming from Agroprom, but that’s a hellishly dangerous path.

Some strange new freaks have shown up around here. From a distance, they look a bit like people, but up close... I once read a sci-fi book where some mujahideen were fighting a bald guy over some spices he was absolutely obsessed with. He was monstrously, obscenely fat and ugly. That’s pretty much how I pictured this guy.

Ever heard of Navidson? No, not the one from the book. He was a stalker. He vanished somewhere around here, got caught in a blowout. An interesting fellow, well-read, loved to philosophize. I’m not sure how he got that name, but things happen, I suppose. 

I knew another stalker—a real social butterfly, the life of any party and yet his name was Lone Wolf. Go figure. Why on earth would they call him that? Damned if I know. 

At least everyone knows the story behind your nickname; Toad spilled the beans, heh-heh.

Word is that local gangs are in touch with certain stalkers, paying them for information and that the whole operation is run by Snitch. He’s a shady little character who hangs out at the Bar; for the right price, he can dig up any dirt you need. He even helps traders get rid of troublesome stalkers. \n\nActually, I wouldn’t be surprised if he ends up putting a hit on these bandits himself. They talk way too much. Take the "Cheerful Tourists," for instance. They’ve already skedaddled off to Agroprom. Their boss, Traveler, clearly knows which way the wind is blowing. He must have caught a whiff of what’s coming.

An interesting scene played out here recently. A raid on a bandit from the "Rippers" gang. Those "Rippers" are absolute scum; they only recruit people who aren't quite right in the head. Sadistic bastards, the lot of them. Good thing there’s one less of them now. With any luck, someone will get to the rest, too, and the Zone might become a little safer.

A military expedition got wiped out somewhere nearby, though, it’s unclear exactly how. In the southern part of the Zone, no one can really go toe-to-toe with a squad of military stalkers; the local mutants aren't up to the task, and the local rookies certainly aren't either. Yet, someone managed to take them down. I intercepted their transmissions to command, but, unfortunately, I couldn't triangulate their position.

Duty lost an entire squad somewhere nearby. They probably went to help those military stalkers and ended up meeting the same fate. What, you hadn't heard? A group of military stalkers got wiped out around here not long ago. What were they even doing in this hellhole? Maybe they’ve come to crack down on the stalkers?

Ah, the Garbage. A good place that brings back memories. I haven't been here in ages, not since I was a rookie making my first forays toward the North. Back then, even the Garbage felt like the "North." 

It’s good here — in the sense that it’s a total shithole. It reeks, it’s radioactive, it’s crawling with bandits and goddamn mutants; but all this crap feels so… familiar. Further north, the stench is worse, the radiation levels are higher, and instead of bandits with double-barreled shotguns, you’re hunted by military stalkers armed with machine guns. And the mutants… well, they’re far more dangerous; just look at the chimeras, for starters. 

Everything, as they say, is relative.

I’d advise you to steer clear of the local stream. Up north, jelly anomaly leaks into it, whether from pipes or somewhere else, who knows. It’s only a matter of time before the whole stream turns into jelly, and believe me, you don’t want to be standing in it when that happens.

Strange things happen here at night. Unknown signals keep popping up on PDAs, you can pick up cryptic radio chatter, and sometimes you’ll see lights glowing by the stream to the north. Someone’s clearly holding secret meetings… but why go to such lengths?

What, did you fall for Ferret’s tall tales too? He claims the Garbage is overflowing with riches, just waiting to be scooped up. He’s lying. You’re better off steering clear of him — he’s a real piece of work, sent plenty of stalkers to an early grave just to serve someone else’s agenda. He’s also got a cozy little arrangement with the local bandits.

Keep your eyes peeled, or you’ll end up paying the price. I nearly got caught off guard by some military stalkers the other day: the bastards opened fire, but I gave them a proper taste of their own medicine; didn’t even hesitate to use a grenade. I didn’t bother finishing them off, though. Those types are always capable of some nasty trick, no better than the Monolith fanatics. Not worth the risk. Besides, landmines are a part of their standard-issue gear.

It’s nice here — like a resort. This place used to be swarming with gangs: the "Rippers," some "tourists," even a bunch of Satanist bandits who called themselves "Priests." Now, it’s just small-time riffraff; nothing but scavengers, really.

Did you hear that the “Duty” faction is looking for a missing squad around here? I saw them: for some godforsaken reason, the whole lot of them wandered straight into an acid fog and kicked the bucket. I’m left wondering: are they just complete fools, or should I look into getting some neurostimulators? I’ve got a hunch that a Controller might be behind this.
You’d better ask someone younger; old timers like us rarely wander this way, and if we do, it’s only for something very important. So, I’ve got no idea, honestly.
Make sure to toss your bolts often — otherwise, you might end up like Cosmonaut, get launched straight into the stratosphere by a gravity anomaly, heh-heh-heh.

I once guided a scientific expedition. They were an unusual bunch — not the typical physicists or biologists you usually see around here, but engineers, experts in some technical field. Can you imagine? They came into the Zone specifically to survey the local tunnels. 

They hauled in a mountain of equipment and thank goodness they were issued exoskeletons; I wouldn’t have lasted long carrying that stuff on my own back. They took a look, ran some scans, scribbled a few things in their little notebooks, and then took off. Never came back, either. Turns out, there’s nothing interesting in those tunnels at all. 

Their gear just picked up some passages leading deeper underground, but you’d need industrial-grade explosives to reach them.

About the Garbage? Well, I’m new around here, so I can’t tell you much. Huh? Why are you shaking your head? Isn’t this the Garbage? Damn… where are we, then? I was trying to reach the Bar by taking a roundabout route, but my PDA ran out of juice and that’s where my maps were. \n\nYou’ve heard of the Bar, right? Well, get this — they turned me away! Said something like, "no place for rookies here." Some stalkers they are... Now I don’t know what to do; I have no clue where I am. Gotta stay on my toes since you can’t step into the same river twice. That’s what Plato said. Or was it Socrates? Damn, it’s like I got smacked in the head; and I only just got kicked out of the philosophy department, too!

I’ve been getting some strange text messages and more than one, actually! There are plenty of bandits around here, that’s for sure. I’ve run into their kind back on the other side of the cordons. They’d strip you clean, and out here, with no law to hold them back, they’ve clearly lost their damn minds. They greet you with bullets first, then talk later! If it were up to me, I’d give them all a good thrashing.

Someone really ought to put up some signposts around here; I have no damn clue how I ended up here or how to get out. The atmosphere is rotten, and the people are just as bad. Nothing but shady characters! The kind that makes you want to hide in the bushes; plus, swarms of mutants. \n\nGood luck to both of us, man. Maybe we’ll cross paths again, if we manage to make it out.

If I were you, I’d steer clear of all these half-finished buildings. Everywhere you turn, you hear people talking in criminal slang. And then there are these restless, undead-looking things: they barely move their limbs, but man, can they shoot! As if that weren’t enough, some shady characters are posting threats online. A new gang, maybe? \n\nGuys with more experience told me: don’t come here. And if you do, know that there’s nothing good to be found — just scum, mutants, and lunatics.

Barely made it out of those ruins in one piece. Listen, friend, take some advice: stay away from here! Some freaks open fire on anyone who passes by! You’d better get out while you can; those extraterrestrial trinkets aren’t worth it. They spun a yarn about a goldmine, but conveniently left out the part about the competition.

Word is, there’s something interesting at a small homestead nearby. Everyone talks about it, everyone knows it’s there, but nobody goes near it. Someone’s clearly watching the place. On top of that, there’s a pack of massive mutts prowling around. They’ll scramble your brain first, then devour you while you’re helpless. I didn’t dare go, but you look like an experienced guy, so maybe you can handle it.

Is the weather always like this here? Everything I’ve got is damp, and you can’t even stop to rest cos you’d get taken out in a heartbeat; there’s no shortage of people looking to do just that. Ugh, it’s suffocating. The only thing worse is an actual "blowout." And the worst part is, it’s only this miserable right here; just a couple of kilometers to the west, things ease up a bit. Mind you, if you walk around long enough, you start to get that metallic taste in your mouth, but that’s pretty much everywhere around here. Go a bit further, though, and bam! Next thing you know, you’re glowing like a Christmas tree. \n\nThat’s probably why there’s no such thing as an old stalker. Have you ever met one? Neither have I.

Hell if I know. I’m sick to death of this cursed fog. It keeps me constantly on edge. You’re always half-expecting some monstrosity to come leaping out at you. Or something even worse — a goddamn human being. And you know what? The longer nothing happens, the scarier it gets. We need to get out of here, and fast.

What the hell? You’ve got some nerve, man. What kind of question is this? Alright, since you’re asking, I’ll tell you a little bedtime story. 

So, once upon a time, in the darkest parts of the Dark Valley, there was a gang of some seriously tough guys who called themselves the "Dead Men," and life was good for them. They’d shake down stalkers left and right; even the Dutiers gave them a wide berth. These highway bandits could have lived happily ever after, but then their boss, in a fit of booze-fueled madness, decided to pick a fight with some military stalkers. The whole gang ended up dead for absolutely nothing. Though, word has it that a few of them, realizing how things were going, managed to bolt. 

So, that’s the story, and here’s the moral: it’s best not to mess with military stalkers.

Keep your eyes peeled, bloodsuckers love to set up their lairs in these ruins; it’s damp here, just the way they like it. If you see the grass getting flattened or the bushes rustling for no apparent reason, open fire immediately — it’s a lot easier to get away from a wounded one. Just pray you don’t run into a whole pack, or you’re done for.

A military stalker has even been spotted around here. They rarely venture this far south, but lately… well, first they showed up at the Garbage, then they were prowling around the Agroprom, and now they’ve made it all the way to the Valley. My partner, may he rest in peace, mentioned seeing one near the utility shed on the east side. I don’t know what caught their interest there, but you’d best stay away. They’ll take you out.

I ran into some ecologists the other day. They’ve been walking around, scouting. There’s some kind of radiation seeping up from the ground here, or at least there used to be. It’s impossible to make heads or tails of what those eggheads are saying; they babble on and it sounds like a proper human language, and you might even catch a familiar word here and there, but the whole thing is completely incomprehensible. 

Anyway, there’s this radiation that presses on your brain, like a ringing in your ears. If you ever feel that, get the hell out of there, and fast. 

The first time I wandered into these parts, I thought I’d finally lost my mind. I guess that’s why all these "sub-humans" roam around here: creatures that are nothing more than empty shells of people.

People who dream of getting rich at someone else’s expense flock here, looking for some kind of "tough-guy" romance. Just remember: nothing but riffraff hangs around here, with the rare exception of passersby like you and me. That’s all there is to say about this place.

I know you won’t find this spot on any map, so I’ll give you the short version: there are two gangs operating in the southern sector: the "Black Slugs" and the "Marlboro Cowboys." Both groups are nothing but trash, but they can still cause you a world of trouble. You might be able to find common ground with the "Blacks" if you know their code, but the "Cowboys" are completely unhinged. Word is, back in the day, they’d set ambushes, strip you of your gear, and force you to work off your own ransom—but these days, they just kill without rhyme or reason. 

There’s an unfinished building by the road from the Scrapyard that serves as a staging ground for all sorts of lowlifes. They pour in here like a river, swelling the ranks of the local gangs. Further on, there are some hangars on the northern side. Don’t go near them, and definitely don’t poke your nose inside: some shady characters were hanging out there, and for all I know, they might still be. I’ve got no desire to check. 

To the east, there’s a complex sealed off by a heavy door. Not many people know what’s inside, and I’m certainly not one of them. Lately, some lowlife thugs have been guarding the entrance; word is, it’s a remnant of the "Dead Men" gang, hiding out there after the guys in uniform, the ones with the colored callsigns, gave them a proper thrashing. 

Further south, there’s a waste dump, and up on the high ground, a couple of ruined farmsteads where anomalous activity is off the charts. That’s about it.

What’s there to say? You can see for yourself. I don’t want to stick around here a second longer than I have to—there’s danger lurking behind every bush. Some dangers have rotten teeth, some have fangs, and others are completely invisible. \n\nAnyway, time is money.

Whatever you do, don’t stray from the path — only do so if it’s an absolute necessity. One step to the left or right, and you’re dead. I’m not joking. You’ll remember my words soon enough. And keep an eye on your PDA; if you see signals from the bandits, get your weapon ready immediately. The thugs around here are rabid: they’ve even been known to broadcast threats over the local comms network. Where else have you ever seen something like that?

If the trader hadn’t dangled some cash in front of me, I wouldn’t have set foot in this place. What really caught my interest, though, was the fact that there’s an old laboratory complex here. It’s been sitting empty since the seventies… or so it seems. You see, there was a rumor going around about a way down into the basement, with a reinforced, armored door at the end. \n\nThe door’s locked tight, obviously, but getting inside… well, there’s bound to be something in there, just waiting to be found. I’m not the only one worried that it might be some kind of terrifying, never-before-seen weapon. If that fell into the wrong hands — game over. It ought to be blown to bits, just to be safe, before some greedy, opportunistic types manage to break in.

You probably already know that this place attracts all sorts of lowlifes. Back in the day, there was a gang here, an old-school one that went by the name "Dead Men." They were the stuff of Zone legend, as far as bandits go. There were about fifteen of them, and they held a base in an administrative building down south. They’d strip seasoned stalkers of their gear, ambush “Duty” squads, and then, whenever they pulled off a big score, they’d go on a massive, destructive bender. That’s actually where the name "Dead Men" comes from: in criminal slang, it’s a term for drunks who’ve passed out completely from booze. \n\nThey were a wild bunch; it was like they had alcohol pumping through their veins instead of blood, driving them to all sorts of reckless feats. Eventually, their luck ran out. They’ve ambushed a group of scientists, stripped some high-ranking egghead of everything he had, killed a few others, and dragged the rest off to hold them for ransom. That brought a whole platoon of military stalkers in APCs down on their heads, and they were wiped out to the last man. Then again, who knows… maybe some of them did survive.

It’s a wretched place—everything’s radioactive, reeking, and stinking to high heaven. Sometimes the fog is so thick it’s like walking through milk. Why did I ever come here? Artifacts. What else would a stalker be after? 

The local thugs have really gone downhill; they shake down newcomers, lost souls who wander in here like moths to a flame. As for the serious stalkers, these punks either steer clear or band together into packs. They’ve got enough courage to gang up five-on-one, but these makeshift groups have zero coordination. 

It’s easy enough to slip away from them, or lure them into an anomaly field and pick them off one by one. You can sometimes scavenge some decent loot from them — stuff they must have taken from someone else, God rest their soul.

I’ve seen plenty of documentation; I even met Journalist once and we swapped some information. 

Just look around. It’s clear that major construction was underway here, and for a good reason. They intended to level that ridge, the one with the drainpipe. Then raze the abandoned hamlets. They had plans for all sorts of facilities scattered about, which would have formed a massive research complex… but then the station blew, and the project was scrapped. 

Still, there was some kind of activity here for a long time afterward, which means there’s still plenty to scavenge.

I spent some time observing the local rats, trying to figure out where they were coming from. Turns out, they don’t just infest the underground tunnels — someone’s actually breeding them somewhere around here! Observing your surroundings here is, shall we say, rather difficult. Not least because of certain "individuals" of questionable reputation.

It’s strange that not everyone knows where the "Killers'" clan is based within the Zone. In fact, some don’t even believe such a faction exists. Who do you think was sending all those threatening messages, then?

You need to keep a sharp eye on your surroundings here. You never know where an ambush might be waiting. And if you don’t have a map, it’s incredibly easy to get lost. \n\nPeople don’t usually go around sharing the locations of lucrative spots for free, but since you could just as easily end up dead anywhere around here, I’ll give you a bit of advice: in that low-lying area to the right of the road (the one littered with junk) you can sometimes scavenge a few minor artifacts. There’s a risk of radiation exposure, of course, but nothing a couple of bottles of good vodka can’t handle.

You need to watch not just where you step, but what’s coming toward you, otherwise, you might miss a bullet, or a truck. I happen to know that death trucks pass through here — the very same kind that keep crashing all the time. If I’m not mistaken, that’s the sort of truck they pulled you out of. \n\nSo, look left, then look right — and only then cross the road. Otherwise, the irony might just get you.

What do you want? You one of those "criminal" types? Nah, doesn't look like it. Oh, wait. You’re one of those "Cargo 200" cases, aren't you? Life’s really put you through the wringer if you’ve ended up riding in something like this. Keep your guard up, the trucks like that one tend to drive through here.

You know, I’ve just remembered. A while back, one of the commanders of the military-stalker groups got himself killed. He was the one who led the raid against the "Dead Men." They really gave those guys a thrashing back then. The Dead Men had a leader — a real piece of work, a total scumbag, but he had charisma. He drank like a fiend, and when he was soused, he’d get these wild ideas. And the kicker was, his crazy schemes usually paid off. But this last gamble of his? It turned out to be his undoing. 

I’m not sure how he found out, but a bunch of raw recruits had been assigned to guard a scientific expedition. Among them was a certain general’s son, looking to earn his next rank. It was supposed to be a simple, low-risk trek near the Perimeter, followed by medals, a hero’s welcome, and a bright career path. But the Dead Men were a formidable bunch—no match for a pack of recruits. They swarmed them, wiped out half the group, and snatched the general’s son. 

It was a bold plan, sure, but that general had been through three wars; he refused to negotiate, even for his own flesh and blood. He leaned hard on the "Palette" unit, forced their elite troops into the fight, and even secured an APC for the operation. In the end, the "Dead Men" became dead in the literal sense. The military-stalkers didn't lose a single man, and that young recruit? He got all the medals — plus a dozen more — and was hailed as a true hero. Posthumously, of course. 

The general, naturally, was not satisfied with such an outcome. The commander understood this too; he scattered his men: some took early retirement, others transferred as far away as they could, and a few even headed into the Zone to live as free agents. 

Ah, he should have looked after himself better. He knew full well they were sending him to his death. And all for what? Pride, greed, and someone’s damn rank.

The underground laboratory is crawling with mutants. You ask how I know? I just do. Down here, everything is connected by a network of tunnels. Some are still open, not yet caved in. The cleverer ones slip through, only to end up as part of the scenery. Hardly anyone ever comes back from such excursions, except for... well, that’s none of your business.

The most valuable and interesting thing here is information. And I’m going to find it, no matter what. The puzzle is nearly complete; just a couple of pieces missing. All you have to do, corpse-boy, is stay out of my way. Then, we’ll all find out what’s really going on here.

Open your eyes. What do you think this is, Wonderland? People don’t get killed for no reason, and you’ll end up dead too if you go around approaching everyone like that. Nothing personal, it’s just that, around here, mistakes might not be forgiven. Go in peace.

What kind of entertainment are you looking for? We’ve got plenty: gravitational, thermal... take your pick. How about some cotton candy that tastes like iron? You could go for a ride in a death truck, or even check out the house of horrors. Take your pick.

This is the asshole of the Zone. The only place worse is beyond the Red Forest. It used to be just like that over there, so you’d better thank the Duty and the military for stepping in and bringing some order.
Don’t get on my nerves! As if this lousy weather wasn’t enough—now I’ve got you pestering me with questions, too.
